title: Best Perfect Aire Dehumidifier (2026): 22 to 150 Pints
dek: A quietly reliable brand with its own supply chain — and one recall detail every secondhand buyer should know.
description: The best Perfect Aire dehumidifier for every space, from the 22-pint flat panel to the 150-pint industrial unit, plus reliability data and the 2021 recall.
intro: A **Perfect Aire dehumidifier** rarely gets the shelf attention of a GE or Frigidaire, yet the brand quietly earns one of the best reliability results in the category. In Consumer Reports’ latest brand survey, Perfect Aire shares the top predicted-reliability tier with Midea, Keystone and Toshiba — and unlike those three, it isn’t built by Midea.

Today’s lineup is built around a slim **flat-panel** design in 22-, 35- and 50-pint sizes, plus a pump version of the 50 and a wheeled 150-pint industrial machine for job sites. It’s a tidy range that covers everything from a bedroom to a warehouse.

There’s one thing to know before you shop, especially used: older Perfect Aire models were part of a large 2021 fire-hazard recall, and today’s model names differ from the recalled ones by a single letter. We’ll show you exactly what to check.
topPicksLead: For most basements and large rooms, the **Perfect Aire 50-Pint Flat Panel** is the one to buy, with enough capacity for an open basement and a direct-to-drain hose connection.

products.name: Perfect Aire 22-Pint Flat Panel Dehumidifier (3PFD22)
pros: Slim flat-panel body suits bedrooms and offices
cons: Retailers disagree on its coverage area
Too small for a damp basement
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the entry point to the flat-panel line and the most popular Perfect Aire model for good reason: it’s sized for the rooms most people actually need to dry — a bedroom, closet or small home office — without taking over the floor.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 278 kWh a year, which is modest for a machine that may run most of the summer. Coverage claims vary wildly between retailers, from about 430 to 1,500 square feet for the same unit, so size it by room type instead: think one bedroom or office, not a whole floor. For other small-room options, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Perfect Aire 35-Pint Flat Panel Dehumidifier
pros: Rated for spaces up to 3,000 sq ft
cons: Drain hose needs a lower outlet
products.whyWeLoveIt: The 35 is the middle step for a living room, large bedroom or the finished end of a basement — more water removal than the 22 without the bulk of a 50-pint machine.
products.performance: Perfect Aire rates it for up to 3,000 square feet with two fan speeds. There’s no pump, so either empty the tank or run a continuous-drain hose to a floor drain below the unit. If you’re torn between sizes, our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) walks through the math.

products.name: Perfect Aire 50-Pint Flat Panel Dehumidifier (1PFD50)
pros: Rated for up to 4,500 sq ft
Backed by a top-tier brand reliability score
cons: Model name is one letter off a recalled model
products.whyWeLoveIt: Fifty pints is the sweet spot for a typical damp basement, and this unit pairs that capacity with a brand that Consumer Reports members rate among the most reliable — without relying on the same factory as Midea and its many badges.
products.performance: Perfect Aire rates it for up to 4,500 square feet using R32 refrigerant, with a hose outlet for continuous drainage to a floor drain. Depending on the retailer, it’s sold as the 1PFD50, 3PFD50 or 4PFD50. Compare it with other brands in our [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) roundup.
products.notes: The recalled 2009–2017 model was the 1PED50 — note the E. New stock isn’t affected, but read the label carefully on any used unit.

products.name: Perfect Aire 50-Pint Flat Panel Dehumidifier with Pump (3PFDP50)
pros: Built-in condensate pump pushes water up and out
Same 50-pint, 4,500 sq ft rating as the standard model
cons: Pricing varies a lot between retailers
Pump adds a part that can fail
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your basement drain isn’t downhill from where the dehumidifier needs to sit, the pump turns this into a set-it-and-forget-it machine that can push water to a sink or out a window.
products.performance: Capacity and coverage match the standard 50-pint unit; the pump simply adds installation flexibility. Shop around — this model’s price swings more between stores than most. See other self-draining options in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.name: Perfect Aire 150-Pint Industrial Dehumidifier (1PACD150)
pros: Continuous drain, humidistat and auto-defrost standard
cons: Overkill for any single room in a home
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is a different animal from the flat-panel units — a rugged, wheeled machine for job sites, warehouses and water-damage cleanup where you need serious extraction and mobility.
products.performance: Auto-defrost lets it keep working in cooler spaces, and continuous drainage means no tank to babysit. It sits outside the 25–74 pint range named in the 2021 recall. For other heavy-duty choices, see our [best commercial dehumidifier](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/) list.

blocks.text: Perfect Aire was launched in 2012 by Bigwall Enterprises, a home-comfort company based in Countryside, Illinois, that designs and distributes its own air conditioners, dehumidifiers and ductless systems.

sections.heading: How we pick the best Perfect Aire dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don’t run a lab. We compared Perfect Aire’s published capacity and coverage ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and retailer spec sheets, then cross-checked brand reliability against Consumer Reports’ member survey and model numbers against CPSC recall notices.
Where retailer specs disagreed — as they do on the 22-pint unit’s coverage — we flagged it rather than picking the most flattering number. Each pick is matched to the room size it genuinely suits.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Perfect Aire dehumidifier

items.label: The right capacity
items.text: 22 pints for a bedroom or office, 35 for a large living space, 50 for most basements, 150 only for commercial jobs.

items.label: Pump or gravity drain
items.text: Pay for the pump model only if your drain sits higher than the unit. Otherwise a hose to a floor drain does the same job.

items.label: The full model number
items.text: On any used unit, read every character. PED and PADP prefixes appear in the recall; PFD and PFDP do not.

items.label: Room-based sizing
items.text: Coverage figures vary by retailer, so size by the room’s dampness and use rather than a single square-footage claim.

items.label: Placement
items.text: Flat-panel units are slim but still need open air around them. See [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Perfect Aire dehumidifiers at a glance
Perfect Aire dehumidifier recall: what to check

blocks.text: In August 2021, the CPSC announced a recall of roughly 2 million dehumidifiers made by New Widetech and sold under several brand names — including De’Longhi, Ivation, Danby, TCL, Kenmore, Haier and Friedrich — after 107 reports of overheating or fire and about $17 million in property damage. The affected units were sold roughly from 2009 through 2017.
The eight recalled Perfect Aire models

blocks.title: New stock is fine — used units need a closer look
blocks.text: Current flat-panel models use 1PFD, 3PFD and 4PFD prefixes and were built after the recall window. But PED and PFD are easy to misread, so check the full model number and manufacture date on any yard-sale, inherited or marketplace unit before plugging it in.

sections.heading: Perfect Aire dehumidifier reviews: is it reliable?

blocks.text: Perfect Aire’s reliability result is more meaningful than it looks. Consumer Reports surveyed 11,944 members who bought 13,632 dehumidifiers between 2014 and 2025, and only four of 23 brands earned the top predicted-reliability score. Three of them — Midea, Keystone and Toshiba — come from the same Midea factories. Perfect Aire reached that tier with a separate supply chain, which makes it a genuinely independent data point.

That doesn’t make any one unit bulletproof. Across all brands, about one in five dehumidifiers develops a problem within four years, so keep the receipt, register the warranty and follow a simple [maintenance routine](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/).

The **Perfect Aire 50-Pint Flat Panel** is the best pick for most basements and large rooms, backed by a reliability score that stands on its own. Choose the **22-Pint Flat Panel** for a bedroom or office, the **50-Pint with Pump** when your drain is above the unit, and the **150-Pint Industrial** for commercial work. Buying new sidesteps the 2021 recall entirely — but if a Perfect Aire comes to you secondhand, read that model number letter by letter. To see how the brand compares with others, visit our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) ranking.

faqs.q: What is the best Perfect Aire dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most basements, the 50-Pint Flat Panel. Choose the 22-Pint Flat Panel (3PFD22) for a bedroom or office, the 35-Pint for a larger living space, the 50-Pint with Pump (3PFDP50) if you lack a low drain, and the 150-Pint Industrial (1PACD150) for job sites.

faqs.q: Is the Perfect Aire 22-pint flat panel dehumidifier any good?
faqs.a: For a single small room, yes. It’s ENERGY STAR certified with a rated 278 kWh a year and a slim footprint. Just ignore inflated coverage claims — it’s a bedroom or office unit, not a basement machine.
Perfect Aire is a brand of Bigwall Enterprises, a home-comfort company in Countryside, Illinois. Unlike Keystone, GE, hOmeLabs and Toshiba, it isn’t part of the Midea-built family.

faqs.q: Is Perfect Aire a reliable brand?
faqs.a: By Consumer Reports’ latest survey, yes. It was one of four brands out of 23 to earn the top predicted-reliability score, alongside Midea, Keystone and Toshiba.

faqs.q: Has a Perfect Aire dehumidifier been recalled?
faqs.a: Yes. The August 2021 New Widetech recall named eight older Perfect Aire models: 1PED30, 1PED50, 1PED50S, 1PED70, 1PEDP50, 1PEDP70, PADP50 and PADP70, sold roughly 2009–2017. Current flat-panel models aren’t included.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Perfect Aire dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Start with the model’s product page on Perfect Aire’s website, searching by the full model number printed on the label on the back or side of the unit. If you can’t find it there, the brand’s customer service can help — and having the exact model number ready also lets you confirm it isn’t a recalled unit.
